the customer was billed for a managed service task that was not executed, an
approved service credit from the same billing cycle was omitted, or the account
was mapped to the wrong rate schedule under the current agreement. Adjustments
are not issued because the customer's forecast was lower than the final usage,
because traffic volume increased unexpectedly, or because a project became more
expensive than planned.

mechanism should have been used. Support checks whether the account met the
usage-band threshold defined in its service agreement for the full billing
cycle, whether a scheduled promotional discount was active during that period,
and whether the customer's service package allowed bundled rate treatment across
multiple managed environments. If the conditions were not continuously met,
support explains why no discount was applied.

## Symptoms

Use this article when a Canon PIXMA MG3620 produces poor print quality such as
streaks, blotches, banding, or uneven color after normal cartridge checks. The
goal is to document safe corrective steps and determine when the defect has
persisted long enough to justify warranty handling.

## Safe troubleshooting steps

Start by confirming whether the issue appears on both plain-text pages and photo
prints. Ask the customer to print a nozzle check pattern and keep the page as
evidence. If gaps or smearing appear, the customer can run one standard head
cleaning, wait five minutes, and print a second nozzle check. If the pattern is
still poor, one deep cleaning cycle is acceptable. Support should not ask the
customer to repeat cleaning over and over, because excessive cleaning consumes
ink without resolving a hardware defect.

## Symptoms

Use this article when a Samsung QN90A owner reports intermittent screen
flicker, brightness pulsing, or rapid flashing that disrupts viewing. The goal
is to separate input-related behavior from a likely panel or control-board issue
without asking the customer to open the television or perform unsafe hardware
work.

## Safe checks the customer can perform

Ask the customer to note whether the flicker appears on every source or only on
one device. A useful first check is opening the TV home menu or a built-in app;
if flicker is visible there as well, the problem is less likely to be caused by
an external cable or player. For external sources, the customer can reseat the
HDMI cable, try a known-good cable, and temporarily set the source output to a
standard refresh rate such as 60 Hz.
